The Creed

What we confess, in one voice, before every kickoff.

We believe in one beautiful game, the pitch almighty, maker of all fixtures and friendlies, of all things visible and replayed on VAR. We believe in one ball, round and true, begotten not made, of one being with the boot; through it all goals were made. For us and for our salvation it came down from the bootroom, was struck by the laces, and became goal.

The Football Evangelists exists because the match report has grown cold and the hot take has grown lukewarm. Somewhere between the expected-goals spreadsheet and the transfer rumour mill, the wonder went missing — so we built a cathedral where it could be found again. Here, a gegenpress is a spiritual discipline, a Cruyff turn is a small resurrection, and a last-minute equaliser at a rain-soaked away end is preached as exactly what it is: grace, undeserved and unrepeatable.

We hold these truths to be self-evident: that a well-weighted through ball is a form of charity; that the low block tests the faith of even the devout; that no player shall be slandered beyond what is meet, for they too are fearfully and wonderfully made — even the centre-forward who has not scored since the Feast of St. Stephen. We do not deal in gossip, only gospel. We do not do transfer rumours; we do revelation.

So come as you are: season-ticket saint or armchair agnostic, ultras' curate or casual pilgrim. Bring your doubts about the referee — we have several of our own, written down and indexed. Take a pew. The sermon is about to begin, and extra time is never guaranteed.

RC

Reverend Rowan Crossbar

Rowan once scored a hat-trick in a five-a-side friendly and has dined out on it for eleven years. He writes about tactics with the serene confidence of a man who has never successfully coached anything larger than a Subbuteo XI. He lives above a defunct sports bar, which he describes, without irony, as “dwelling above my church.”
